questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Permutation
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for ${}_{n}{P}_{r}$ is given by

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}\,.
$$

Substituting $n=9$ and $r=4$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{9}{P}_{4} & =\frac{9!}{(9-4)!} \\  & =\frac{9!}{5!} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot \cancel{5!}}{\cancel{5!}} \\  & =9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6 \\  & =3\,024\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Diana is choosing a $4$-digit passcode for her cellphone from the digits ${1,2,3,4,5,6},$ where no digit is used more than once. How many different passcodes are possible?
questions.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $6$ digits, so $n=6.$ We want to select $4$ of those digits for the passcode, so we have $r=4.$ 

Therefore, the number of different passcodes is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{6}{P}_{4} & =\frac{6!}{(6-4)!} \\  & =\frac{6!}{2!} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot \cancel{2!}}{\cancel{2!}} \\  & =6\cdot 5\cdot 4\cdot 3 \\  & =360.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Ashley has $5$ tasks. She decides to do one on Thursday and another on Friday. How many different choices of the two tasks does Ashley have?

The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$

There are $5$ tasks to choose from, so $n=5.$ We want to select $2$ of those for Ashley to do, so we have $r=2.$ 

Therefore, the number of different choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{5}{P}_{2} & =\frac{5!}{(5-2)!} \\  & =\frac{5!}{3!} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 4\cdot \cancel{3!}}{\cancel{3!}} \\  & =5\cdot 4 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$
